Hazard Ratio of a WCE Model

Source: R/wceGPU.R
HR.Rd

Computes, from a model fitted by wceGPU(), the hazard ratio between two exposure histories.

HR(object, vecnum, vecdenom, level = 0.95)

Arguments

object

A wceGPU object.

vecnum

Numeric vector: the exposure history of interest (numerator of the HR), in reverse chronological order: the first value is the exposure at the current time, the second the exposure one time unit earlier, and so on. A vector longer than the cutoff of the model is truncated, and a shorter one is padded with zeros (no exposure further back in time).

vecdenom

Numeric vector: the reference exposure history (denominator of the HR), in the same order and with the same length rules as vecnum.

level

Level of the bootstrap confidence interval of the HR (default 0.95).

Value

A one-row matrix with the HR and, if bootstrap() was called on object, the lower and upper limits of its bootstrap percentile confidence interval.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Dataset
drugdata <- WCE::drugdata

# WCE model with bootstrap (example with 20 bootstraps)
cutoff <- 90
wce_gpu <- wceGPU(data = drugdata, nknots = 1, cutoff = cutoff,
                  id = "Id", event = "Event", start = "Start",
                  stop = "Stop", expos = "dose",
                  covariates = c("age", "sex"),
                  constrained = FALSE, aic = FALSE, confint = 0.95,
                  x = TRUE)
wce_gpu_bootstrap <- bootstrap(wce_gpu, R = 20)

# Exposed at a dose vs. unexposed
exposed   <- rep(1, cutoff)
unexposed <- rep(0, cutoff)

HR(wce_gpu_bootstrap, exposed, unexposed)
} # }
